name: Cookiemator
author: RaMGoN

sections.description:
Cookiemator is a lightweight, complete, self-hosted and 100% free solution designed to comply with the European GDPR, the ePrivacy Directive and the cookie guidelines of the Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD) on WordPress, with no external monthly subscriptions and no paid versions.

Unlike other solutions that limit essential features or charge per number of visits, Cookiemator offers all of its advanced tools unlocked from day one, keeping the data on your own server and taking care of your site’s performance.

Main features

  • 100% free and unlimited (no Pro version, no subscriptions): All features are included at no cost, with no monthly pageview limits, no mandatory watermarks and no need to connect your site to external paid dashboards.
  • Two-layer compliance (AEPD and GDPR guidelines): First-layer banner with “Accept all” and “Reject all” buttons of identical size, color and visual prominence (no dark patterns), plus a “Settings” button in third position.
  • Multi-tab preferences modal (second layer): Pop-up window with Consent, Details and About cookies tabs, granular toggles per category (Necessary, Preferences, Statistics, Marketing) and a close (X) button in the top right corner.
  • Preventive blocking of scripts and iframes: Automatically intercepts non-essential scripts (analytics, advertising pixels, heatmaps) and external iframes (YouTube, Vimeo, Google Maps) until the visitor gives explicit consent.
  • Native Google Consent Mode v2: Emits the default and updated signals (ad_storage, ad_user_data, ad_personalization, analytics_storage and personalization_storage) directly in the <head>.
  • Hybrid cookie catalog (automatic WP-Cron scanner + manual editor): Periodically scans your site’s HTML and active cookies via WP-Cron (daily, weekly or monthly), and also lets you add, edit or delete cookies manually.
  • GDPR audit log in the database: Records each user consent in your own database with a unique UUID and an anonymized IP address, ready to export as CSV for any inspection or legal request.
  • Optimized for performance and Core Web Vitals: Clean, ultra-light code with no heavy external dependencies, so it does not slow down loading or cause layout shifts (CLS).
  • Design, colors and texts 100% customizable: Adjust button colors, backgrounds, borders, corner radius, typography (inheriting your theme’s font or using Google Fonts), logo and every text in the banner and modal.
  • Built-in shortcodes: Use [rgcookies_link] to reopen the preferences modal from anywhere and [rgcookies_declaration] to display the categorized cookie declaration table on your Cookie Policy page.

External services

This plugin does not send any data to external servers by itself. However, it allows the site administrator to optionally configure the conditional loading (strictly after the user’s consent) of the following third-party services:

  • Google Fonts: If the administrator selects a Google font (Inter, Poppins, Roboto, Montserrat) instead of inheriting the theme font, the stylesheet is loaded from https://fonts.googleapis.com (Google Privacy Policy).
  • Google Analytics 4 / Google Tag Manager / Google Ads: If the administrator enters their tracking IDs in the plugin settings, the scripts connect to https://www.googletagmanager.com only after the visitor accepts the corresponding category (Google Privacy Policy).
  • Meta Pixel (Facebook): If a pixel ID is configured, it connects to https://connect.facebook.net after Marketing consent is granted (Meta Privacy Policy).
  • TikTok Pixel: If a pixel ID is configured, it connects to https://analytics.tiktok.com after Marketing consent is granted (TikTok Privacy Policy).
  • LinkedIn Insight Tag: If a Partner ID is configured, it connects to https://snap.licdn.com after Marketing consent is granted (LinkedIn Privacy Policy).
  • Microsoft Clarity: If a project ID is configured, it connects to https://www.clarity.ms after Analytics consent is granted (Microsoft Privacy Statement).
  • Hotjar: If a site ID is configured, it connects to https://static.hotjar.com after Analytics consent is granted (Hotjar Privacy Policy).
sections.installation:
1. Upload the cookiemator folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory, or install it directly from the WordPress plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin from the “Plugins” menu in WordPress.
  3. Go to the Cookiemator menu in your WordPress admin panel to customize colors, logos and texts, and to run the cookie scanner.
sections.faq:
Is it really 100% free, or are some features locked behind a paywall?

It is completely free. There is no Pro version, no hidden payments, no monthly subscriptions and no limits on traffic volume or pageviews. All advanced features (Google Consent Mode v2, automatic script and iframe blocking, the hybrid WP-Cron scanner and the audit log exportable to CSV) are included and unlocked for all users.

Does it comply with the current AEPD guidelines and the European GDPR?

Yes. Cookiemator has been designed following the technical criteria of the Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD) and the GDPR: “Accept all” and “Reject all” buttons in the first layer with identical visual prominence, real preventive blocking before consent, granular selection by category and a record of consent evidence.

Do I need to create an account on an external service or pay a monthly fee?

No. The plugin is 100% self-hosted. All processing, the cookie catalog and the audit log are stored directly in your own WordPress installation, without relying on external platforms or sharing your visitors’ data with third parties.

How does the Google Consent Mode v2 integration work?

The plugin natively integrates the official Google Consent Mode v2 parameters (ad_storage, ad_user_data, ad_personalization, analytics_storage and personalization_storage). It sends the denied state by default before loading the tags and updates it dynamically as soon as the user accepts their preferences, with no complex configuration needed.

Does it slow down my site (performance)?

No. The frontend code is optimized to use minimal resources and avoids heavy libraries. You can also choose to inherit your own theme’s typography to avoid additional external requests.

How do I add a link to reopen the cookie settings panel in the footer or on the Cookie Policy page?

You can insert the shortcode [rgcookies_link text="Cookie settings"] or add a custom link in any WordPress menu pointing to #cambiar-cookies.

How do I display the categorized cookie declaration table on my Cookie Policy page?

Insert the shortcode [rgcookies_declaration] inside the content of your Cookie Policy page. The table is updated automatically with the active cookies in your catalog.
sections.changelog:
1.1.1

  • Rewrote the readme.txt in English (short description, description, installation, FAQ, screenshots and changelog) to comply with the WordPress.org plugin directory requirements.
  • Tested up to WordPress 7.2.
  • Updated the plugin version and asset version strings.

1.1.0

  • Accessibility (WCAG) and SEO improvements for Google PageSpeed Insights: replaced the <h4> tags of the banner and modal titles with neutral semantic <div> containers to avoid skipped levels in the page heading hierarchy.
  • Adjusted the style of the direct “Settings” link in the WordPress plugins list.

1.0.9

  • Added a “Settings” shortcut in the WordPress plugins list with the native admin style.

1.0.8

  • New built-in vector icons in the admin panel (side menu and header), official screenshots and full documentation.

1.0.7

  • Interface adjustments and graphic assets.

1.0.6

  • Stability improvements and general optimization of the scanner and the audit log.

1.0.2

  • Updated the plugin name and slug for submission to WordPress.org.
  • Enqueued styles and scripts, and improved handling of requests and custom scripts.
  • Fixed the admin menu label and tab navigation.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
